title: Re-Dating Anchor for a Passed Due Date on a Reclassification After Death (Occupancy and Residency Certification)
content:
When an Occupancy and Residency Certification profile is reclassified after a certifying borrower's death and its open cycle's due date has already passed, the passed due date is re-dated from a **re-dating anchor**. The anchor is fixed as follows:

| Records on the reclassification date | Re-dating anchor |
|---|---|
| the primary borrower has an accepted health-care absence notice on file | the date the death notice was received (the surviving borrower, in care, could answer only once the death was reported) |
| the primary borrower has no accepted health-care absence notice on file, and the death came on or after the open cycle's due date | the date of death |
| every other case — no such notice, and the death came before the open cycle's due date | the reclassification date |

The death notice read is the accepted death notice on file for the profile received most recently, with the date of death it states and the date it was received.

## Points of judgement

- The first row turns only on whether the primary borrower has an accepted health-care absence notice on file; where one is, the receipt date of the death notice is the anchor whatever the date of death.
- In the second row a death on the due date itself counts as coming on or after it.
- *Hypothetical case.* No health-care absence notice is on file for the primary borrower and the death notice states a date of death some weeks before the open cycle's due date: neither of the first two rows applies, so the anchor is the reclassification date.
